item.title: Topic Overview
item.description: Spiking Neural Networks Spiking Neural Networks, or SNNs, are neural networks that communicate with discrete spike events instead of continuously passing dense activation values through every layer.

item.title: Spiking Neural Networks
item.description: Spiking Neural Networks Spiking Neural Networks connects Topic Overview with 1.

item.title: 1.1 Why Spiking Neural Networks Exist
item.description: Why Spiking Neural Networks Exist Imagine a tiny camera on a battery-powered robot watching a hallway. Most of the time, the hallway barely changes.

item.title: 1.2 Biological Inspiration Without Biological Overclaiming
item.description: Biological Inspiration Without Biological Overclaiming After why spiking neural networks exist, biological inspiration without biological overclaiming becomes the next question to resolve.

item.title: 1.3 The Leaky Integrate-and-Fire Neuron
item.description: The Leaky Integrate-and-Fire Neuron Imagine the event-based sensor from the previous idea watching a quiet scene.

item.title: 1.4 Spiking Network Architecture
item.description: A single spiking neuron can already do something powerful: it can sit quietly, accumulate incoming signals over time, and fire a spike when its internal state reaches a threshold.

item.title: 2.1 How SNNs Learn
item.description: How SNNs Learn Imagine a spiking network already knows how to compute with brief events: each neuron waits, accumulates input, and emits a spike when its internal state reaches a threshold.

item.title: 2.2 Surrogate Gradient Training
item.description: Surrogate Gradient Training Imagine a spiking network that already knows how to listen for events: a neuron receives incoming spikes, its internal voltage rises, and when that voltage crosses a threshold it emits its own spike.
